item.title: Micheal Jacobs Named Second Team All-SWAC
item.description:
BIRMINGHAM, Ala. | Guard Micheal Jacobs was named to the Southwestern Athletic Conference (SWAC) Men's Basketball Second Team, the conference announced on Friday morning.
The Atlanta, GA. native averaged 17.6 points, 5.1 assists and 3.7 rebounds in 29 games played. He posted a career-high 30 points vs. Prairie View and added a personal-best 10 rebounds (at Marquette) and 10 assists (at Jackson and vs Alabama A&M) this season. He scored over 20 points 14 times this season and finished with seven or more assists seven times this season.
Jackson State's Daeshun Ruffin was selected as the SWAC Men's Basketball Player of the Year, while Alabama State Jerquarius Stanback earned Defensive Player of the Year Honors.
Joining Ruffin on All-SWAC first team was Dontae Horne (PVAMU) Jakobi Heady (BCU), Quion Williams (UAPB) and Micheal James (MVSU).
All-SWAC second team was Kintavious Dozier (Alabama A&M), Micheal Jacobs (Southern), Troy Hupstead (Texas Southern), Daniel Rouzan (Bethune-Cookman) and Tai'Reon Joseph (Prairie View).

item.title: Jaguars Rally Late to Secure Thrilling Comeback Win Over Alabama State on ESPNU
item.description:
BATON ROUGE, La. | Southern University men's basketball delivered a dramatic finish Monday night inside the F.G. Clark Activity Center, erasing a second-half deficit and closing with poise to earn a 69-68 comeback victory over Alabama State in front of a crowd of 5,127.
Trailing by as many as 12 points in the second half the Jaguars (11–13, 7–4 SWAC) stayed composed, tightened defensively, and made winning plays down the stretch to secure the one-point victory on national television.
Southern dominated the paint and the glass throughout the night, scoring 32 points in the paint and holding 34-22 rebounding advantage, while also forcing key turnovers late to swing momentum.
DaMariee Jones helped anchored the comeback finishing with 12 points and 12 rebounds, for his fifth double-double of the season. Jones also knocked down two clutch free throws with just over five minutes remaining to give the Jaguars the lead and fueled Southern's late run.
Micheal Jacobs delivered a steady all-around effort scoring 11 points, dishing out six assists, and coming up with a crucial steal in the final minute to help set up the game-winning sequence. Jacobs also went 7-of-8 from the free-throw line, keeping Southern within striking distance throughout the second half.
AJ Barnes and Terrance Dixon Jr. added 12 and eight points respectively, while Cam Amboree chipped in eight points, helping Southern receive balanced contributions across the lineup. The Jaguars also shot 90.9 percent from the free-throw line in the second half.
With the game tied late, Fazl Oshodi who was 0-of-5 from behind the arc delivered the defining moment. Knocking down a go-ahead three-pointer with 6.3 seconds remaining to put Southern in front for good.
The Jaguars then closed the game with a defensive stand, sealing a hard-earned conference win.

item.description:

An intense rivalry that had 6,489 fans inside the Mini Dome was amplified towards the end with a wild finish as Southern Michael Jacobs was fouled with 0.8 seconds on the clock as he was shooting a layup that would send him to the line for game-winning free throws. But before he could attempt the free throws a double technical foul was issued to the Tigers head coach and he was ejected from the game.
Cam Amboree stepped up to the charity stripe to shoot the technical foul free throws and knocked down four consecutive free throws, giving the Jaguars a 64-60 lead. Jacobs then stepped up to the charity stripe and made his first free throw, extending the SU advantage 65-60. Before he could attempt his second free throw another technical foul was issued to GSU. Amboree then stepped back up to line and knocked down to more free throws. Jacobs missed his final throw, and the game ended on a GSU rebound.
Forward DaMariee Jones led the Jaguars tying his season-high with 15 points, going a perfect 7-of-7 from the floor. He also added nine rebounds. Cam Amboree contributed 13 points, four assist and two steals. Joe Manning finished with 10 points.
Antwan Burnett led the Tigers with 15 points and 14 rebounds, Kintavious Dozier added 13 points.
Southern had the lead for 33 minutes in the contest, which saw the score tie once late in the second half. The Jaguars largest lead was 12 points after Joe Manning three point make.
With 2:58 remaining in the contest, Dionjahe Thomas made two free throws to extend SU's lead 58-50.
P.J. Eason's free throws pulled the Tigers within a point, 58-57 with 1:16 left on the clock. The next possession DaMariee Jones layup pushed SU's advantage to 60-57 with 1:08 left in the game. Stepping up to the line to convert the old-fashioned three-point play and extend the game to a two-possession advantage he missed the free throw.
Off the missed jumper by the Tigers, Jones came up with a big defensive rebound and passed the ball to Michael Jacobs who was immediately fouled by GSU with 28 second left. Jacobs missed the front end of the one-one free throw but got his own rebound, then SU turned the ball over with 25 seconds.
After a GSU timeout, Mikale Stevenson knocked down a game-tying three pointer with 13 seconds remaining in the game. On the next SU possession, Jacobs drove to the basket and was fouled with 0.8 seconds left in the game. With three technical fouls and an ejection being assessed to the Tigers, the Jaguars were awarded a total of eight shots at the charity stripe in which they made 7-out-8 to end the ballgame.

item.title: Southern University Athletics Mourns the Loss of Former Jaguar Basketball Legend Bob Love
item.description:
CHICAGO, IL | Former Southern University and Chicago Bulls forward Bob Love, a three-time All-Star who spent 11 years in the NBA, died Monday night. He was 81.
The Bulls said Love died after a long battle with cancer.
Growing up in northern Louisiana (Bastrop), Love was one of 14 children. He was nicknamed "Butterbean" because he liked lima beans.
The 6-foot-8 Love starred at Southern University in Baton Rouge from 1961-1965. He is the all-time leading scorer in Southern University Men's Basketball history with 2,458 points (23.7 average) and finished with 1,483 rebounds (14.7 average) during his 104 games at SU.
During the 1965 season, Southern made it to the Elite Eight NAIA National Tournament before falling to Ouachita Baptist 65-64. Bob Love Scored 138 points in the 3 games he appeared in the 1965 NAIA National Tournament.
Love also earned NAIA All American honors during his illustrious career at Southern. His #41 jersey was retired in 2012 and can be seen in the rafters of the F.G. Clark Activity Center.
"Southern University and the basketball word lost a great one," said director of athletics Roman Banks, who is also Love's godson. "Bob was a class act on and off the court and was the first NBA player to come from Southern all while dealing with a severe speech impediment which he overcame and went on to become an inspiration in the community."
He was selected by Cincinnati in the fourth round of the 1965 NBA draft. He played for the Royals for two seasons before he was picked by Milwaukee in the expansion draft in 1968.
Love and Bob Weiss were traded to Chicago in November 1968 for Flynn Robinson. With the Bulls, Love developed into one of the NBA's best forwards.
Love averaged 21.3 points and 6.8 rebounds during his nine seasons with the team.
"With his No. 10 jersey hanging in the United Center rafters, his on-court achievements are forever etched in history, but Bob's impact transcended basketball," the Bulls said in a statement.
"He became an inspirational figure and a passionate community ambassador for the Bulls, dedicating himself to charitable causes and uplifting countless lives with his motivational speeches.
Love was an All-Star for three straight seasons in 1970-73. He averaged a team-high and career-best 25.8 points during the 1971-72 season.
Love retired after the 1976-77 season. He averaged 17.6 points and 5.9 rebounds in 789 career games, also playing for the Nets and Seattle SuperSonics.
In January 1994, Love became the second player in franchise history to have his number retired by the Bulls, joining Jerry Sloan. Love was part of the team's inaugural Ring of Honor class this year in January.

item.title: Former SU Basketball Star Carlos Sample was Selected LABC Mr. Louisiana Basketball Award Winner
item.description:
Sample starred as a two-time All-Southwestern Athletic Conference player at Southern from 1987 to 1990, where he helped guide the Jaguars to three consecutive SWAC Regular Season Championships (1988, 1989, 1990), two consecutive SWAC Tournament Championships (1988, 1989), two consecutive NCAA Tournament appearances (1988, 1989) and one NIT appearance (1990). He scored 1,399 points (16.3 avg.) and handed out 472 assists (5.5 avg.)
BASKETBALL WAS A LOT MORE THAN WINS FOR SAMPLE
By: Robin Fambrough Written for the LABC
BATON ROUGE, LA – What Carlos Sample saw in the Scotlandville High gym on a Sunday night last month made him smile.
"We were coming back from a weekend trip, so I stopped by the gym," Sample said. "There were youth basketball games going on and I saw three of my former players out there coaching."
"The wins, the championships and all that stuff is great. But to see former players out there, working with kids and giving back? It's about more than playing basketball. That will end … it's about preparing for life."
Make no mistake about it, there were plenty of wins and championships for Sample, who is being honored as Mr. Louisiana Basketball by the Louisiana Association of Basketball Coaches.
Sample will receive the award during the LABC's 50th Annual Awards Banquet on Saturday, May 4, at the Baton Rouge Marriott. It is the most prestigious annual award given by the LABC and is presented annually to someone who has made a significant, long-term contribution to the game of basketball at any level in the State of Louisiana.
Sample coached the Hornets to an incredible 14 straight title game appearances in the Louisiana High School Athletic Association's highest classification, Class 5A/Division I select, before stepping down after the 2022-23 school year. Sample continues to work as athletic director at north Baton Rouge-based Scotlandville.
"He's very deserving … I can tell you that," said Kenny Almond, the 2014 Mr. Louisiana Basketball recipient and a legendary coach in his own right. "Look at what he has done. He has done a great job coaching and he always did it the right way."
"Carlos could change the style of offense they played to fit the players he had. Believe me, there is a lot to that. Tough defense was part of it. He had talent, but when he coached, his players got better."
Scotlandville won eight LHSAA state titles, had six runner-up finishes and led three nationally-ranked teams during Sample's 16-year stint at the school, winning 85 percent of his games with a 482-83 record. The Hornets won their first title in 2012 and eventually earned the moniker, "The Program".
Before coming to Scotlandville, Sample spent nine seasons at his alma mater, Istrouma. He has an overall winning percentage of 77 percent and an overall record of 676-198 that also includes one season at Livonia. Those totals also include 12 district titles and 10 East Baton Rouge tournament titles.
The number of Division I Scotlandville players Sample coached started with J.J. Thomas (UL-Lafayette) in 2011 and includes current Virginia star Reece Beekman, the star of Sample's 2020 Division I select champions. Guards such as Beekman and Javonte Smart typically come to mind as top players for Sample, a star guard in his own right at both Istrouma and Southern University.
A 6-foot-10 post player, Damian Jones, currently plays for the Cleveland Cavaliers after a college career at Vanderbilt. Sample's first college signee was Istrouma post player Anthony Greenup, who forged a different professional distinction.
"Getting kids to see there are possibilities they never thought about, like going to college, is a big part this," Sample said. "My first player to go to college was Anthony Greenup. He ended up playing for the Harlem Globetrotters and traveling around the world".
"I could be hard on them (players). The lessons you learn in basketball … working hard and being disciplined … go beyond basketball."
All in all, Sample produced two high school All-Americans, four Louisiana Gatorade Players of the Year and eight Class 5A state players of the year.
Rival coaches, such as Madison Prep's Jeff Jones, laud Sample's accomplishments.
"There are only two guys I have been around who have the ability to have their kids do exactly what they want them to do," Jones said. "And that's Carlos Sample and Harvey Adger (Glen Oaks coach). Their teams don't make a lot of mistakes and they are detail oriented."
"I was an assistant (at Glen Oaks) when Carlos was at Istrouma. He was someone I wanted to model my program after."
Others see Sample's 14 consecutive title game appearance as more than just a one generational standard.
"What he (Sample) did was raise the bar," said Liberty's Brandon White, whose team won the Division I select title in March. "I don't think you'll see that again – 14 straight title games – especially in 5A."
Prior to beginning his coaching career, Sample starred as a two-time All-Southwestern Athletic Conference player at Southern from 1987 to 1990, where he scored 1,399 points (16.3 avg.) and handed out 472 assists (5.5 avg.) Following his senior season, he was named the MVP of the 1990 Louisiana College All-Star Game.
In addition to honoring Sample, the May 4 awards banquet will include the induction of former University of Louisiana at Monroe star Carlos Funchess into the Louisiana Basketball Hall of Fame. There will also be recognition of Louisiana's major college, small college, junior college and high school players and coaches of the year, along with the top pro player from the state, as well as the presentation of the LABC's Don Landry Award to former long-time Northwestern State University coach and athletic director Tynes Hildebrand. item.title: Kevin Johnson Named Finalist for Ben Jobe National Coach of the Year

BOSTON, MA -- The 25 finalists for the 2023-24 Ben Jobe National Coach of the Year award have been announced. The award is presented annually to the top minority head coach in division I college basketball.
Kevin Johnson, who was named the 15th head coach in program history on March 29, 2023. In his first year guiding the Jaguars he led them to 18 wins, the most wins since 2016 season. He is just the sixth head coach in SU history to win 17 games or more during his first season. Coach Johnson is the only SWAC coach during the 2023-24 season to knock of a top #25 ranked team (#21 Mississippi State on 12/3/23) and to earn a quadrant 1 win. The Ben Jobe award is named in honor of one the most iconic coaches in the history of basketball at Historically Black Colleges and Universities. He is best known as the head coach of Southern University, a position he held for 12 seasons. He was also head coach at Alabama A&M, Alabama State, Talladega, Tuskegee, and South Carolina State.
His record at Southern was 209-141 and included four NCAA Tournament appearances. He also coached the Jaguars to one NIT appearance, five SIAC championships, 11 SWAC titles and two NAIA Tournament Championships. Perhaps his most memorable moment as a coach was leading No. 13 seed Southern to a 93-78 win over No. 4 Georgia Tech in the first round of the 1993 NCAA Tournament. It stands as one of the great upsets in the history of the event.
Coach Jobe passed away on March 10, 2017.
The recipient of the annual award is determined by a 10-member voting committee, which consists of current and former head coaches, as well as two senior staff members of collegeinsider.com.

DAYTONA BEACH, Fl. -- Southern dropped a heartbreak in overtime as they suffered their first conference loss Monday night at Moore Gymnasium 83-81.
Southern (9-8, 3-1) had three Jaguars in double figures. Lead by Tai'Reon Joseph with 31 points, two steals and two rebounds. Brandon Davis helped out with 20 points, three rebounds and three assist. Tidjiane Dioumassi finished with 12 points and six assist. Derrick Tezeno added eight points and team high eight assist.
HOW IT HAPPENED Southern jumped out to a 7-0 lead as the first 15 minutes was back and forth contest.
The Jaguars found themselves with a 41-36 lead at the break.
Southern took its then-largest lead of the game 56-42 after Joseph made 3-pointer with 12:43 left in the half after holding the Wildcats scoreless for two minutes.
JaRonn Wilkens free throws extended the lead 71-69 with 21.0 seconds remaining, but the Wildcats hit a contested jumper with 3.0 seconds remaining forcing the game to overtime. Southern made it a two-possession game with two-and-a-half to play in OT on a Brandon Davis layup that made it 78-73, but BCU answered with a layup to make it a three-point game once again.
With 7.1 seconds remaining, Southern pushed the ball down the court. Derrick Tezeno's three missed, but a big offensive rebound and putback by Davis just missed the mark, but a foul was called on the play sending Davis to the line for two free throws.
Davis's first free throw just rimed out. The Jaguars attempted to miss the second shot in hopes of getting an offensive rebound, but it fell into a Wildcats hands as the final horn sounded.
INSIDE THE NUMBERS Southern shot 41.9 percent (26-of-62) from the field, 35.7 percent (10-of-28) from the 3-point line and 67.9 percent (19-of-28) from the free-throw line Tai'Reon Joseph lead the Jaguars in scoring with 31 points, two steals and two rebounds Brandon Davis added 20 points, three rebounds and three assist Tidjiane Dioumassi finished with 12 points and six assist. Derrick Tezeno added eight points and team high eight assist Southern finished with 30 points in the paint, 22 points off 15 Wildcats turnovers, 13 fast break points, 10 bench points and nine second-chance points Bethune Cookman went 25-of-53 (47.2 percent) from the floor, 5-of-16 (31.3) from the 3-point line and 28-of-36 (77.8 percent) from the charity stripe Dhashon Dyson and Jakobi Heady finished with a team-high 19 points BCU finished with 28 points in the paint, 19 bench points, 13 second-chance points, 11 points off seven SU turnovers and seven fast break points UP NEXT Southern will return to action Saturday Jan. 20 as they travel to Grambling State for a 2:30 pm match-up with the Tigers on HBCUGO sports.

item.title: Southern Men’s Basketball Announces 2026-27 Schedule
item.description:
BATON ROUGE, LA. — Southern University men's basketball will face a demanding test from the opening tip of the 2026-27 season as the Jaguars announced their upcoming schedule, featuring a challenging non-conference slate featuring matchups against programs from the ACC, Big East, Big Ten, Missouri Valley, Mountain West, SEC and West Coast. Along with three regular-season home contests at the F. G. Clark Activity Center.
The Jaguars will open the season with one of the more challenging stretches on the schedule, playing five consecutive road games against NCAA Division I opponents. Southern begins the campaign Monday, Nov. 2 at Southern Methodist University before traveling to Texas Christian University on Friday, Nov. 6.
The road swing continues Sunday, Nov. 8 at Drake University, followed by a Tuesday, Nov. 10 match up at Iowa State University and a Thursday, Nov. 12 contest at the University of Minnesota.
"We're excited about the challenges our schedule presents this season," said Southern head coach Kevin Johnson. "Our non-conference schedule will give us an opportunity to compete against some very good basketball programs, and we believe those experiences will help prepare us for the intensity and rigors of SWAC play. We want to challenge our team early, learn from each game and continue to grow as we get ready for conference competition. We're looking forward to the opportunity and can't wait to get the season started."
Southern will return home for its first home contest of the season on Tuesday, Nov. 17, hosting Louisiana Christian University at 11:00 a.m for field trip day game 1. The Jaguars will close out November with another pair of road challenges, traveling to the University of Nebraska on Nov. 25 before facing Vanderbilt University on Nov. 27.
The Jaguars will continue non-conference play in December, hosting Champion Christian College on Tuesday, Dec. 1 at 11:00 a.m. for field trip day game 2, before embarking on another challenging stretch on the road. Southern will travel to Fresno State University on Dec. 5 and later make a trip west for contests at the University of Oregon on Dec. 16, the University of the Pacific on Dec. 18 and the University of California on Dec. 20.
SU closes out its non-conference schedule at home Monday, Dec. 28 against Southern University-New Orleans at 2:00 p.m.
The Jaguars open Southwestern Athletic Conference play on the road Saturday, Jan. 2 at Texas Southern before traveling to Prairie View on Monday, Jan. 4.
Southern will make its home conference debut Saturday, Jan. 9 against Florida A&M. The Jags will remain at home to host Bethune-Cookman on Monday, Jan. 11, followed by Grambling State on Saturday, Jan. 16.
After a pair of road contests at Arkansas-Pine Bluff and Mississippi Valley State, SU returns home to host Alcorn State on Saturday, Jan. 30. The Jaguars will then welcome Jackson State to Baton Rouge on Monday, Feb. 1.
The second half of the conference schedule features road contests at Alabama A&M and Alabama State before Southern returns home for consecutive contests against Prairie View on Feb. 13 and Texas Southern on Feb. 15.
SU will close out the regular season with four road games and two home contests, including a pair of home games against Alabama State on Tuesday, March 2 and Alabama A&M on Thursday, March 4.
The 2027 Southwestern Athletic Conference Men's Basketball Tournament is scheduled for March 8-13 at the Gateway Center in Atlanta, Georgia.

item.title: Southern Lands 168 Student-Athletes On SWAC Commissioner's Honor Roll
item.description:
BATON ROUGE, La. | The Southwestern Athletic Conference has announced its 2025-26 SWAC Commissioner's Honor Roll and Southern Athletics has continued to excel in the classroom with 168 Jaguars earning a spot on that prestigious list.
The SWAC Commissioner's Honor Roll is comprised of student-athletes with a cumulative GPA of 3.0 or higher during the Fall 2025 and Spring 2026 semesters.
Football saw the most student-athletes recognized with 25. Followed by Soccer (24), Baseball (22), Softball (15), Women's Cross Country / Track & Field (15), Men's Cross Country / Track & Field (14), Volleyball (14), Women's Basketball (11), Men's Tennis (7), Women's Tennis (6), Men's Basketball (6), Men's Golf (4), Women's Golf (3) and Bowling (2).
